messages:
tony (Customer): Hi team — our payments integration started seeing 429s on /v1/generate around 03:05 UTC. Error: '429 Rate limit exceeded'. Happening for tenant `acme-fin`, region eu-west-1. Traffic graph shows short spikes to ~1800 RPM for ~20s, then drops. Can you advise?
elaine (Support): thanks — can you paste the request id and a sample response body? also did this start after a deploy or client change? :eyes:
tony (Customer): sample body: `{\"error\":{\"message\":\"429 Rate limit exceeded\",\"type\":\"rate_limit\"}}` request id: `req-8f3a2c` no deploys on our side, but we did roll a new lambda version last night.
support-bot: Alert: tenant acme-fin exceeded minute rate quota threshold at 2025-11-04T03:05:20Z (peak 1798 rpm) — auto-notify sent to #support.
rafa (SRE): quick checks: are they reusing ephemeral tokens per invocation? lambda scale-up + token refresh race can cause stampedes. also check for HTTP/2 multiplexing from their proxy — many concurrent streams map to multiple API calls that count toward RPM.
pranav (Eng): can you share a minimal curl that reproduces the 429? also rough concurrency (# of lambdas active) and whether they use streaming responses. for token reuse issue we usually see many fresh Authorization headers pushed at once.
tony (Customer): reproducer (non-prod):
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
We run this from multiple containers during deploy. Concurrency ~150 containers for short bursts.
elaine (Support): that explains it — short fanout bursts across many containers will blow the per-minute window. two quick mitigations: 1) add jitter/randomized backoff during rollout; 2) implement a small token cache per container to avoid issuing new bearer tokens per request.
rafa (SRE): from infra side we can: a) temporarily raise soft quota for acme-fin for 30m while they rollout; b) route a small percentage to a lower-capacity fallback model to reduce token pressure. if raising quota, need PO approval.
pranav (Eng): suggested client-side fixes in order: 1) cache tokens per container/process for 60s, 2) limit parallelism of the deploy script (batch pods into groups of 10-20 with 500-1000ms random delay), 3) convert bursty fanout to a lightweight queue (SQS/kafka) to smooth minute-buckets.
tony (Customer): ok will patch deploy scripts and add token cache. can you put in the soft quota bump for 30m so we don't hit production during rollback?
elaine (Support): filing internal request: "soft-quota bump for acme-fin" — linking SRE. Rafael, assigning to you for temporary elevation.
rafa (SRE): ack — submitted quota bump to infra: request id qreq-442. increased minute window from 1200 -> 3000 for 30 minutes starting now. monitoring ETA ~2m.
support-bot: Quota change applied for tenant acme-fin (3000 rpm) — change id qreq-442. Monitoring alerts adjusted.
tony (Customer): seeing fewer 429s already, thanks. we'll deploy the jittered rollout in next 15m and confirm. :thumbsup:
elaine (Support): follow-up checklist for thread: - confirm patched deploy avoids new 429s for 1h - send postmortem w/ root cause (lambda scale + token refresh pattern) - recommend long-term: client token caching, rollout batching, and SDK change to expose local token reuse.
pranav (Eng): adding a short snippet we recommend for node lambdas:
```
// minimal in-memory token cache
let cached = { token: null, exp: 0 };
async function getToken() {
  if (Date.now() < cached.exp) return cached.token;
  const t = await fetchTokenFromAuth();
  cached = { token: t.value, exp: Date.now() + 45_000 };
  return cached.token;
}
```
Use 45s so you don't rely on last-second refresh.
tony (Customer): will implement and report back in 30m. thanks everyone."
